newsitem.title: UK: Man puts Ivory cocoa arrivals at 740,000 T by Jan.
newsitem.headline: Man puts Ivory cocoa arrivals at 740,000 T by Jan.

text.p: Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals are estimated to have reached 740,000 tonnes by January 27, 100,000 tonnes lower than the same period last year, according to a report by E.D.&F. Man Cocoa received on Monday.
The report, the summary of which was published last week, said arrivals from February to end-April was expected to total just over 150,000 tonnes, giving a total main crop of around 900,000 tonnes.
The estimate compares with Man's estimate for main crop arrivals of 1.54 million tonnes between October 1995 and end-April 1996. Their estimate based on the tree crop was 980,000 tonnes for 1995/96.
Man projected the Ivorian mid-crop at around 150,000 tonnes "but this is dependent on favourable weather during February and March" it said.
The estimate for the total Ivorian crop was 1.050 million tonnes compared with 1.220 million in 1995/96 based on arrivals. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom 44-171-542 8072
